extracted.intended_audience: general readers of literary sketches and aspiring humorists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit criteria for composing short humorous literary sketches: aim to amuse through genial characterization, quaint detail, gentle anecdotes, and social ritual scenes rather than to instruct. Emphasizes tone, audience-sensitivity, and picturesque effect over strict authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write to please rather than to instruct
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is so much pleasanter to please than to instruct--to play the companion rather than the preceptor.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author defends amusement as a legitimate aim: the only real harm in failing is the writer’s own disappointment. Successful humorous writing should at least 'rub out one wrinkle from the brow of care' or 'beguile the heavy heart of one moment of sorrow' and prompt a benevolent view of human nature. Frame the piece as convivial company rather than a lesson; set modest, affective goals (cheer, lighten, humanize).

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor genial good-humor over pungent wit
rubrics_metrics.description: “Wit, after all, is a mighty tart, pungent ingredient, and much too acid for some stomachs; but honest good-humor is the oil and wine of a merry meeting, and there is no jovial companionship equal to that where the jokes are rather small and the laughter abundant.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying solely on sharp, acerbic, or highly pungent jokes that may alienate readers. Prefer mild, inclusive, and plentiful small jokes that generate broad, warm laughter. Be sensitive to audience taste; excess 'acid' wit is an anti-pattern for the convivial tone advocated here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make kindness and benevolence the source of delight
rubrics_metrics.description: “The joyous disposition of the worthy squire was perfectly contagious; he was happy himself, and disposed to make all the world happy…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray warm, benevolent characters whose good temper spreads to others; humor derived from kindness and generosity produces genuine, contagious enjoyment. Character warmth is a reliable basis for sympathetic comedy rather than ridicule or malice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use quaint/antiquarian detail for comic color and atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrator delights in 'odd and obsolete things' and in 'a quaintness ... suited to the time and place'; customs (wassail bowl, mummery, maskings) give 'peculiar zest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ specific, picturesque antiquarian details and vanished customs to create atmosphere and gentle comic interest. Such particulars can charm readers and lend authenticity of mood even when they are strange or obsolete; they function as scenic humor rather than factual exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit character contrasts to produce comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: “The two college chums presented pictures of what men may be made by their different lots in life.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juxtapose people shaped by different circumstances (prosperous squire vs withered parson, young romp vs ancient household) to highlight absurdities and produce comic effect. Contrasts in temperament, fortune, and habit serve as an economical device for gently satiric observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer innocent, genuine hilarity to broad coarse revelry
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the old hall 'may have resounded...with many a scene of broader rout and revel, yet I doubt whether it ever witnessed more honest and genuine enjoyment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value scenes of simple, honest merriment over coarse, bawdy, or offensive revelry. The piece favors conviviality and warmth; excessive grossness or vulgarity is an anti-pattern for the author's comedic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage communal rituals and games for physical and social comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of wassail, blindman’s-buff, maskings, mummeries, and dances are used to create uproar and merriment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shared rituals, seasonal customs, and group games as scaffolding for comic scenes: they provide opportunities for physical comedy, costume-based humor, role-play, and ensemble interplay. Such communal activities anchor humor in social practice and generate lively episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize picturesque effect over strict historical authenticity when serving comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: “The costume, to be sure, did not bear testimony to deep research, and there was an evident eye to the picturesque…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy of costume or antiquarian detail is secondary to visual and comic effect. If a slight inauthenticity enhances the picturesque or the laugh, it is acceptable. The aim is atmospheric clarity and entertainment rather than scholarly exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use self-aware narration and audience-framing to set comic expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrator anticipates 'the questions asked by my graver readers' and defends writing that amuses rather than instructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-commentary and addressing reader expectations can establish tone, disarm criticism, and align the audience with the author’s purpose. Framing remarks about the work’s intent help normalize lightness and invite readers to enjoy rather than scrutinize.
